extracted.intended_audience: journal peer reviewers / subject-matter experts who review manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Best-practice guidance for academic journal peer reviewers on how to evaluate manuscripts responsibly, ethically, and constructively across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should refrain from reviewing a manuscript if there is any conflict of interest (e.g., a manuscript authored by a former Ph.D. student or close collaborator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not proceed with peer review when a clear conflict exists; decline the assignment. The page lists the example of a former Ph.D. student or close collaborator as situations that require not proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect timelines and avoid unnecessary delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must respect timelines and avoid unnecessary delays, while also ensuring the review is thorough and not rushed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not procrastinate reviews for weeks or months; likewise, do not complete a review in minutes. Balance timeliness with adequate time to examine the manuscript and supplementary materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough examination of supplementary and supporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully examine all supplementary and supporting data provided with the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include supplementary files and appendices in your evaluation to verify claims, reproducibility, and integrity; skipping these sections is listed as a common mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality must be maintained throughout the process; the contents of the manuscript should never be shared, discussed with others, or used for personal gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not discuss the manuscript with third parties or use unpublished ideas/data for your benefit. Maintain confidentiality both during and after the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness, objectivity, and avoidance of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review must always be fair, objective, and unbiased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid bias based on race, nationality, institution, language proficiency, or other irrelevant factors. Present critiques based on the work's merits only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report suspected scientific fraud or plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer suspects scientific fraud, data manipulation, or plagiarism, they should promptly report these concerns to the journal editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to investigate publicly; inform the editor with specific concerns and supporting observations (e.g., image manipulation signs, inconsistencies in data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer role: scientific evaluation, not copyediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers need to understand that they are not copyeditors; their primary role is scientific evaluation, not language polishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus feedback on scientific validity, methodology, interpretation, and integrity. You may note language issues, but substantive editing/copyediting is not the primary expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance novelty vs inclusivity according to journal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify whether the manuscript offers novel insights when the journal prioritizes groundbreaking research; if the journal emphasizes inclusivity or incremental advances, weigh that context in your evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your subject-matter expertise to determine whether the work introduces fundamental advances or incremental improvements, and consider the journal's stated priorities (examples: Nature vs Cureus journals). Also check literature to prevent duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect cited literature for existence, relevance, and recency
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect all published literature cited by the manuscript to ensure the cited work exists and that recent and relevant literature is appropriately cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm citations are accurate; ensure controversies and differing viewpoints are presented in the literature review in an unbiased way. Flag missing key references or over-reliance on outdated sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research problem clarity and addressing a gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the research problem sufficiently clear, and does it address a well-known research gap?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the authors clearly state the problem and contextualize its importance within the field; unclear problems should be identified and authors asked to clarify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods sufficiency to address the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the methods employed sufficient to address the research problem?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the study design, experimental procedures, and analyses are appropriate to test the hypotheses or answer the research questions posed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design robustness (sample size, controls, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the study design (including but not limited to sample size, controls, etc.) robust?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check sample sizes, control groups, randomization, blinding, and other design features. Flag underpowered studies or improper controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and Methods detail and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the Materials and Methods section detailed so other researchers can reproduce the experiments after going through this section?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure protocols, reagents, datasets, and analytic pipelines are described or referenced sufficiently; request more detail or data/code sharing when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess for obvious study bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the study show any obvious bias?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify selection bias, measurement bias, confirmation bias, or other systematic issues that could invalidate results or interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors used rigorous statistical methods?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate appropriateness of statistical tests, handling of multiple comparisons, assumptions checks, effect size reporting, confidence intervals, and transparency about analytic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results and presentation accuracy, clarity, and non-misleading figures/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the results (including the figures, tables, and graphs) accurate, clear, and not misleading or ambiguous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that figures/tables match reported numbers, axes/scales are appropriate, and no selective presentation or manipulation obscures interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide intelligent, actionable recommendations for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Would you like to make any intelligent recommendations for improving the quality of work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete, evidence-based suggestions (e.g., additional analyses, clarifications, experiments) that would strengthen the manuscript rather than vague criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess importance and fit to journal standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the presented results advance the field of study in some way, and does the importance of the advance match the journal standards?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh novelty/impact relative to the journal's aims and scope; recommend revisions or rejection consistent with that assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for research integrity issues (fabrication, image manipulation, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you see any obvious research integrity issues (data fabrication, image manipulation, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for duplicated/blotted images, impossible values, inconsistencies between reported and raw data; report concerns to editors with supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure conclusions are supported by results
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the discussed results lead to the stated study conclusion(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that claims in the Discussion/Conclusion sections are proportional to the data presented and that authors acknowledge limitations and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request additional expertise or decline if outside expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers can write to the journal and request additional review if they are not familiar with certain aspects; if the research lies significantly outside their expertise, they must not participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack competence on key methods/areas, notify the editor and either request a co-reviewer/second reviewer or decline the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common mistakes to avoid (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of frequent reviewer mistakes to avoid including: reviewing despite clear conflict of interest; rejecting without furnishing valid reasons; finishing review within minutes; procrastinating; contacting authors directly; skipping Methods/supplementary; failing to verify conclusions or cited work; ignoring exaggerated conclusions or limitations; using unprofessional language or unfair criticism; overlooking ethical approvals or data integrity issues; ignoring non-compliance with journal guidelines; allowing bias based on race/nationality/institution/language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist to self-audit your review before submission. Each listed item is a concrete anti-pattern that undermines review quality and fairness; avoid them and flag problems to editors when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review checklist: cross-check, format, clarity, constructive evidence-based feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing the evaluation, reviewers should cross-check assessments for omissions, draft the review in the format recommended by the target journal, and communicate observations using clear, scientific, and unambiguous language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comments are consistent with your overall recommendation, provide constructive evidence-based feedback, maintain confidentiality, and verify you did not miss key issues before submitting the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check compliance with scope, formatting, and journal policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that manuscripts have been initially screened by editors for scope, formatting, and policy mandates, but reviewers should check compliance with the journal's scope and policies as they evaluate the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag non-compliance the editor missed (e.g., ethics approvals absent, policy violations, major scope mismatches) and remind authors/editors of required corrections or disclosures.
